item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00085","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C03","C18","C15"],"selected_candidate_label":"C03","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C03 plausibly supplied the drafting framework for the later commemorative proclamation: a sequence of policy-oriented recitals, a presidential designation of a recurring observance, an appeal for public participation during the designated period, and a further exhortation explaining the civic purpose of participation. The subject and duration changed from cancer control for a month to honoring the flag for a day, but the operative ceremonial machinery is materially parallel. C18 also uses a recital-to-public-call-and-further-urge structure, but it does not designate a formal observance. C15 shares proclamation form and exhortatory language but performs a materially different land-management function.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"do hereby direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings on June 14, 1948, and I call upon the people of the Nation to observe that day as Flag Day by suitable ceremonies and by the display of the flag","parent_excerpt":"do hereby set apart the month of April 1948 as Cancer Control Month; and I invite the Governors ... to issue similar proclamations","explanation":"Both operative openings formally designate the 1948 observance and immediately solicit organized participation."},{"child_excerpt":"I also urge all citizens to reflect upon the responsibilities which this banner enjoins as well as the privileges it carries","parent_excerpt":"I also invite the medical profession, the press, the radio, the motion-picture industry, and all organizations and individuals ... to unite during the month of April","explanation":"Both add a second public exhortation specifying how citizens and institutions should give substantive effect to the observance."},{"child_excerpt":"Whereas ... it has properly become a national custom to observe the anniversary ... by public and private ceremonies","parent_excerpt":"Whereas by a joint resolution ... the Congress authorized and requested the President to issue annually a proclamation setting apart the month of April as Cancer Control Month","explanation":"The recitals in both establish the basis for a recurring national observance before the formal designation and public appeal."}]}
